podcast.body: Freddie Fender wrote this song in 1967, and various singers, including Linda Martell, recorded it. His English and Spanish recording in 1974 garnered significant attention from country radio, leading it to number one on both the Billboard Country charts and the Billboard Pop Chart in March 1975. Fender initially didn't want to record it, believing it wasn't "rock and roll enough." "But if he ever breaks your heart, if the tear drop ever starts, I'll be there before the next cheer drop falls."

podcast.body: "Before the Next Teardrop Falls" was a country pop crossover hit for Freddie Fender. This song is used as a benchmark for catchy songwriting, compared to Ben Peters' work on Charlie Pride's "Kiss An Angel Good Morning." "another country pop crossover that Freddie Fender made a hit before the next cheer drop falls."
